list: the official 55 trophies, as published on PlayStation
note: Route lines, steps, hints and every estimate in this dossier were written fresh around the official 55-trophy list. Hours and difficulty ratings are the author's own estimates, and the in-game trackers remain the authority on every count, medal and percentage.

phases.name: Green Light
phases.goal: Clear the opening mission and take full control of Leonida.
phases.about: The route starts where the story starts. Nothing else on the list is reachable before the opening mission is done, so this short phase exists to get every player onto the same page.

phases.name: Story Run: Chapters 1-3
phases.goal: Push the campaign through the first three chapters.
phases.about: A straight march down the main mission markers. Required missions that fall inside this stretch are collected here so the story route stays a single, uninterrupted line of work.

phases.name: Story Run: Chapter 4 & Finale
phases.goal: Finish the last numbered chapter and the closing mission.
phases.about: The story ends here, and with it every mission-type trophy on the list. Keep optional work on hold; the atlas deliberately leaves the open-world sweep for after the credits.

phases.name: Street Work & Heists
phases.goal: Work the crime loop: robberies, heists, heat and odd stunts.
phases.about: With the story tools in hand, the crime economy is fully open. This phase batches every robbery, wanted-level stunt and vehicle oddity so the money and the mischief share one block of play.

phases.name: Stranger Strands
phases.goal: Close out the named stranger strands and their odd moments.
phases.about: Each strand is a short campaign of its own. Running them as one phase keeps the map logic coherent and feeds both the strand-count trophy and the strange-moment unlocks at the same time.

phases.name: Activities & Skill Checks
phases.goal: Clear the volume and skill trophies: stunts, races, ranges and challenges.
phases.about: The largest pure-playtime block. These are repeatable systems rather than one-off scenes, so they can be paced across as many sessions as the totals demand.

phases.name: Collections, Property & Completion
phases.goal: Sweep the world and close the 100% completion stat.
phases.about: The long tail. Collections, property, one-off scenes and the completion stat itself live here, and the atlas treats them as the final audit rather than a background task.

phases.name: The Platinum Stamp
phases.goal: Confirm nothing is left, then collect the platinum.
phases.about: No work remains by design. This phase is the audit step: reconcile every counter, then let the last unlock hand over the platinum.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is not a separate task; it is the certificate handed over once the other fifty-four entries are done. Treat it as the final audit rather than an objective, because when the last remaining trophy pops this one appears alongside it. Nothing here can be earned early, bought, or skipped, and no route variation changes that. A tidy checklist kept from the first sitting to the last is the only preparation this needs, and by then it is already earned.
steps: Finish all fifty-four other trophies
Reconcile the in-game trackers one final time
Collect the platinum alongside the last unlock
trophies.hint: Keep working the list; the platinum has no requirements of its own.
trophies.verification: Confirm in the console trophy list that every other entry shows earned; the platinum follows automatically.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Congratulations! You're a Leonida Legend."
Atlas route phase 8 (The Platinum Stamp) — final audit

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission Gone Fishing is the front door of the campaign, and completing it is the entire requirement. Expect the trophy within the first ten minutes of a fresh save, since the mission leads the campaign and nothing optional can come before it. No side condition is attached to the official wording, so play the objectives in order and let the closing scene run. Every platinum route in this atlas begins here.
steps: Start a new campaign
Play Gone Fishing through its objectives
Watch the closing scene through to the end
trophies.hint: This is the very first mission the game hands you.
trophies.verification: The unlock notification appears as the mission ends; the trophy list records it at once.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Complete Gone Fishing."
Atlas route phase 1 (Green Light) — opening mission Gone Fishing

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter one is cleared by reaching its closing scene, and that scene is the whole trigger. Stay on the main mission markers and let each cutscene finish rather than skipping out mid-flow. The description adds no optional condition, so anything else on the map can wait for the later phases. On any healthy save this should rank among the least risky unlocks on the entire list.
steps: Follow the chapter one mission markers
Complete each mission as it opens
Let the chapter closing scene play out
trophies.hint: The end of chapter one is the trigger, nothing more.
trophies.requires: Unlocks after the opening mission is done — see t2 (Just Like Paradise).
trophies.verification: The chapter transition screen doubles as the unlock moment; confirm the entry in the trophy list afterwards.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Complete Chapter 1."
Atlas route phase 2 (Story Run: Chapters 1-3) — chapter one milestone

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter two is another milestone on the story line: play its missions through, watch the chapter end, and the trophy follows. The official description attaches nothing beyond completing the chapter, so side content can safely wait. The colourful name nods to the money running through this stretch of the plot rather than hinting at a task. Keep every mission running to its end and the unlock is close to automatic.
steps: Continue the story into chapter two
Complete every mission the chapter offers
Collect the unlock at the chapter close
trophies.hint: Finish chapter two and the trophy is yours.

trophies.verification: The unlock fires at the chapter two close; the trophy list entry is the record.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Complete Chapter 2."
Atlas route phase 2 (Story Run: Chapters 1-3) — chapter two milestone

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter three, as its name suggests, carries the campaign into Vice City itself, and the trophy fires when that chapter closes. There is no grind and no choice to make here; plain completion of the chapter's missions is everything. The atlas habit for every chapter trophy applies: never abandon a running mission halfway through a session break. On a normal playthrough nothing can interfere with it, which makes it one of the most dependable ticks on the board.

Complete the chapter's missions in order
Let the ending scene run to the unlock
trophies.hint: Chapter three ends where this trophy fires.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter four is the final numbered chapter, and the trophy unlocks as it closes. The description asks for nothing beyond completion, so the run can stay lean while optional work waits for the free-roam phases. It is also a sensible planning point: this is the moment to decide how the collection sweep after the credits will be scheduled. The unlock itself needs no action beyond finishing the chapter.

Finish the chapter's final scene
Plan the post-credits sweep while the credits roll
trophies.hint: Finish chapter four and the scene does the rest.

trophies.verification: The unlock arrives at the chapter four ending; confirm it in the trophy list.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission is the last gate of the story, and completing it is the whole requirement. Expect a longer set-piece than a routine chapter mission, which is why this gold sits slightly above the chapter ticks in effort. No medal or performance threshold appears in the official wording. Keep resources in reserve for the closing fight and treat the ending scenes as part of the mission.
steps: Reach the story's closing mission
Clear all of its objectives in one sitting
Take the gold unlock at the mission end
trophies.hint: Just the story's closing mission stands between you and this gold.
trophies.requires: Unlocks after Chapter 4 is complete — see t6 (Top Of The World, Ma) so the closing mission can start.
trophies.missable: Required missions are normally replayable after the credits, but replay behaviour is not verified, so avoid deliberately postponing this to the very last sitting.
trophies.verification: The mission-end notification appears and the gold entry lands in the console list immediately.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Complete the final mission."

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a required story mission, so no route can bypass it and no special preparation is needed. Open it from the mission flow, work down the objective list, and let the end screen settle. The official wording sets no performance bar of any kind. For anyone following the chapters in order, this is an automatic tick.

Complete each objective as presented

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a required mission, and completion alone earns the trophy. Heist-style missions often offer a choice of approach, and nothing in the description favours one plan over another, so pick whichever suits your style. Aim to run it through in a single sitting, because abandoning a heist midway is the one habit that can cost you setup progress and force a repeat. The unlock lands at the mission end.

Play the setup and execution objectives
Finish the mission rather than abandoning it

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a required mission somewhere in the middle stretch of the story, and completing it is the entire trophy. This atlas leaves its exact chapter placement to the game's own flow rather than guessing a number. Play it through, let the closing scene run, and move on. No optional condition is attached to the official wording.

trophies.guide: Headliners is another required mission, so the story itself schedules when it appears. The only condition the official wording states is completion. Avoid padding the run with retries for style; a clean finished attempt is all the trophy wants. The unlock arrives at the mission end like the rest of this set.

Complete all objectives in a single run
Collect the unlock at the end screen

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown takes the story to the airport authority, and completing it is the entire trophy. Expect a set-piece pace rather than a stealth exercise. One planning note: the later free-roam airport stunt in the street phase is a different trophy, so do not conflate the two locations while route-planning. The unlock is automatic at mission end.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory reads as a late-story set-piece operation, and its trophy is plain completion of it. Budget a longer session than for a routine mission, since an operation of this scale typically runs multiple stages. No performance threshold appears in the official wording. Finish the end scene and the tick is yours.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story
Work through the full objective list
Collect the unlock after the end scene
trophies.hint: Expect Operation Savage Glory to run long.
trophies.requires: Unlocks after Chapter 3 is complete — see t5 (Vice City, Baby!) so Operation Savage Glory is available.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: One hundred percent completion is the heaviest single item in this atlas and deserves to be run as a project rather than a trophy. The official description does not enumerate what counts, so the in-game checklist is the only authority worth trusting. Open it early, schedule its categories as their own sessions, and re-audit after every batch of content. The genuine hazard is an unlisted requirement surfacing in the final hours, which is exactly why the audit starts on day one rather than in the endgame.
steps: Open the in-game completion checklist early
Clear its categories region by region
Re-audit after each batch and before the platinum push
trophies.hint: Trust the in-game checklist and audit it as you go.
trophies.verification: The in-game completion percentage reaching 100 is the proof; the unlock notification follows it.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Attain 100% Completion."
Atlas route phase 7 (Collections, Property & Completion) — 100% completion stat

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty stunts is a volume figure, and the description reads most naturally as a cumulative count rather than a fixed list of jumps. The simple habit is to hunt a ramp, a hill or a drift line on every drive, because the tally climbs while you do everything else. If the last dozens stall, run a dedicated stunt loop in a fast car across familiar roads. With the background habit in place, one or two dedicated evenings are usually enough to close the figure.
steps: Chain stunts on every drive between objectives
Favour obvious ramps, hills and drift lines
Close the last dozens with a dedicated fast-car loop
trophies.hint: Chain ramps and drifts whenever you drive and the count climbs by itself.
trophies.verification: Watch the running stunt total in the stats screens; the unlock fires at 250.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Complete 250 Stunts."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — stunt system

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The description asks you to try each type of activity once, and since no count is stated officially the in-game activity menu is the definitive type list. Breadth, not skill, is the point: one entered session of each type satisfies the wording. Sampling activities as they appear during the story keeps the work nearly free. Finish with a menu audit so no type is overlooked.
steps: List the activity types from the in-game menu
Enter one session of each type
Cross-check the menu for anything missed
trophies.hint: One brief session of each activity type is enough.
trophies.missable: Activities are presumably always open, but an unknown type could be overlooked late, so keep the menu audit current rather than leaving it to the end.
trophies.verification: No stated counter exists, so confirm by walking the activity menu and checking each type has been opened.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Try each type of activity once."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — activity types

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold in every Shooting Range challenge is a skill trophy, and the atlas advice is to learn before scoring: several drills reward rhythm and target order more than raw reaction speed. Settle loadout and settings first, then climb the list one challenge at a time. Rank it among the stiffer items on the list and give it several short, focused sessions rather than one tired marathon. Because the range is repeatable, a lost evening costs nothing but time.
steps: Learn each range challenge type with practice runs
Chase gold one challenge at a time
Budget several sessions rather than one marathon
trophies.hint: Learn each drill first, then chase the gold scores.
trophies.verification: The range results screens show the medal per challenge; the unlock fires when all show gold.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — Shooting Range

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: A win at every Top Fun drone race location is a tour with a competitive twist: finishing is not enough, first place is. Use the first entry at a new location as a scouting lap, then push for the win once the shortcuts are known. Treat the in-game location list as the checklist rather than trusting memory. A first place at the last location closes the trophy.
steps: Enter a Top Fun race at each location once to learn it
Learn each course's shortcuts early
Convert every location into a first-place finish
trophies.hint: First place at every drone race location is the bar.
trophies.verification: Each location's menu entry shows the best result; the unlock follows the last first place.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — Top Fun Drone Race

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different races means twenty distinct events, not twenty wins of a single favourite. Diversify from the start: rotate across the race categories and locations, keeping a rough tally as you go. Repeating the same event presumably adds nothing, so farming one circuit is wasted effort. Careful pacing matters more than outright speed here.
steps: Spread entries across the race types on offer
Count wins against distinct events, not repeats
Protect a sure lead carefully in the final laps
trophies.hint: Spread the wins across different race events.
trophies.verification: Track the distinct wins yourself; the notification fires on the twentieth.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Win 20 different races."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — street races

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beating Cal is a single rivalry duel inside the fishing activity, not a fishing grind. Work out what the duel measures, size or count, then outperform him on that measure. If a first attempt falls short, the activity format implies a retry, though that is convention rather than a verified fact. One comfortable evening is a generous budget.

Learn what the duel scores
Outperform Cal and take the win
trophies.hint: Outscore Cal once and the trophy is yours.
trophies.verification: The duel result screen is the immediate proof; the notification follows the win.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Beat Cal in a fishing challenge."
Atlas route phase 6 (Activities & Skill Checks) — fishing challenge

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: One completed arcade game is the entire requirement, so pick the cabinet you like best rather than sampling all of them. Play the game to its natural end and let the result screen settle. The description names no score threshold and no specific machine. This is a coffee-break trophy.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet through the arcade activity
Pick the game you find easiest
Play it to its natural end screen
trophies.hint: Pick any cabinet and finish one game.
trophies.verification: The game's own end screen is followed by the unlock notification.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight completed strands is a commitment count, and the silver grade signals the scale. The working rule is to finish what you start, because a half-done strand is progress you cannot bank. Leonida holds more strands than eight, so choose the lines that suit your route and close them one by one. Verify the finished total in the pause menu at the end of every strand so the count never surprises you.

trophies.guide: Three complete card sets is the classic collection loop, and a checklist is essential because a set missing one card is worth zero. Gather cards region by region rather than at random, and reconcile each set's gaps before moving into a new area. Sets are finite, so a missing card is recoverable only by finding it. The third completed set triggers the unlock.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: One hundred WAiNK locations is a traversal trophy, and the practical plan is a delivery route: dense districts first in passing, far corners in one dedicated session at the end. The in-game tracker shows the running total and is the only number worth trusting. The last handful is always the slowest, so budget a final sweep. Keep moving; a steady pace across a few evenings lets the counter do the bookkeeping for you.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Fifty challenges is a volume target rather than a skill wall, and the best treatment is background work: a handful per session across the campaign reaches it without a dedicated grind. Sample every type you meet, finish the ones that suit you, and let the tally grow. The official description states no specific challenge list. The fiftieth completion fires the unlock.
steps: Sample every challenge type you encounter
Finish the ones that suit your build
Tally completions across sessions
trophies.hint: A handful of challenges per session adds up quietly.
trophies.verification: Track completions in the relevant menu; the notification fires at fifty.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Shaking a four-star wanted level alongside your partner is a staged chaos exercise, and the atlas treats it as a planned stunt rather than an accident. Build the heat deliberately in a stretch where your partner is active, because improvising a four-star escape is where attempts go wrong. Choose the getaway route and vehicle before the stars appear. The moment the stars empty while your partner is still along for the ride, the unlock lands.
steps: Raise the wanted level to four stars with your partner active
Plan an escape route and vehicle beforehand
Run the heat down until it clears
trophies.hint: Build the four stars on purpose, then execute a planned getaway.
trophies.verification: The wanted stars clearing while the partner is active, followed by the notification, is the proof.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — wanted-level stunt with partner

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Three shop robberies on a live wanted level is a streak exercise, and the practical shape is a circuit: shops chosen for proximity, robberies triggered in sequence, and heat deliberately kept alive between them. The failure mode is losing the wanted level by accident, so route the run away from ambush-friendly streets. Stage the final escape to begin immediately after the third shop. The intact streak at the end is the unlock.
steps: Pick three shops close together
Trigger the robberies in sequence
Keep the wanted level alive until the third completes
trophies.hint: Keep the heat alive across all three robberies.
trophies.verification: The third robbery completing with the streak intact, followed by the notification.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — shop robbery streak with partner

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: One hundred discovered vehicles is a breadth trophy, and the habit is simple: never take the same model twice when a new one is parked beside it. Common models fill the count early, and the real work is the rare tail, which deserves its own session with the in-game list open. Riding, driving or stealing all count as discovery under the plain wording, so prefer being behind the wheel when something unusual appears. The hundredth discovery fires the unlock.
steps: Vary every vehicle you take across the campaign
Check the discovery list periodically
Hunt the rare tail with dedicated sessions
trophies.hint: Vary every ride and let the in-game list track discoveries.
trophies.verification: The in-game vehicle list shows the discovery count; the unlock fires at 100.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Discover 100 vehicles."
Atlas route phase 7 (Collections, Property & Completion) — vehicle discovery list

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Five takedowns in a single Combat Focus activation is a timing trophy, not a grind. The setup matters more than the shooting: reload before the attempt, find a firefight where enemies cluster, and trigger the slow-motion window only when all five are reachable. A gang clash or a dense story firefight is the natural stage. One clean activation closes it.
steps: Find a firefight with five or more enemies grouped
Activate Combat Focus at the right moment
Take all five down before the meter drains
trophies.hint: One Combat Focus window, five clustered targets.
trophies.verification: The notification fires on the fifth takedown within a single activation.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — Combat Focus combat system

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: An unscheduled departure at VCIA is deliberately open-ended, and the natural reading is an experiment trophy: the game wants you out of the airport by a route no schedule would sanction. The exact method is not stated, so budget exploration time and treat failed ideas as tuition. Save before each committed attempt, because a broken plan should cost a reload and never the session. When the right exit works, the notification settles the mystery.
steps: Explore the VCIA perimeter for access points
Try unusual vehicles and routes out
Save before committed attempts
trophies.hint: Find an exit the flight schedule would never approve.
trophies.missable: If the departure depends on an event, vehicle or access that exists only under some conditions, the window could close; the description confirms neither direction, so run the experiment early.
trophies.verification: The unlock notification on the successful departure; there is no stated counter.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — VCIA free-roam stunt

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a wink at being inside a Rhino tank, and finding one is the actual work. Tanks usually arrive through military sites or staged events, and neither route is confirmed, so the in-game help and world markers are the first places to look. Once a Rhino is available, the scenario the description jokes about is the trigger. Save the access opportunity before using it.
steps: Look for tank access at military or event locations
Check in-game help for how Rhinos appear
Trigger the described scenario with the Rhino
trophies.hint: Getting inside a Rhino is most of the work.
trophies.missable: If Rhino access depends on a location or event that is not always present, the opportunity could pass; that possibility is unverified, so treat any found access as worth saving first.
trophies.verification: The notification fires when the described scenario plays out with the Rhino.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Kinda hot in these Rhinos."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — Rhino tank scenario

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: An undetected jewelry robbery is a stealth run, and the rule is to study before acting: guards, cameras, timing. Move slowly through the whole robbery and use the stealth tools rather than improvising under pressure. If a plan collapses, restart the attempt instead of pushing a detected run to the end, because a detected robbery pays money but not the trophy. One clean pass from entry to exit is the goal.
steps: Study the store's guards and cameras first
Take a slow approach through the robbery
Restart the attempt if detection happens
trophies.hint: Stay unseen from the front door to the getaway.
trophies.missable: If the robbery is a one-time scripted opportunity rather than a repeatable activity, a failed chance might not return; the description does not say whether it repeats, so take the first solid chance seriously.
trophies.verification: The notification fires at the robbery's clean completion; any detection voids the attempt.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Rob a jewelry store without being detected."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — jewelry store stealth robbery

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Five vault robberies with escapes is the heist loop at volume, and the wording makes the escape part of the count: a robbery is not done until you are clear. Find vault opportunities in the world and the crime listings, run them one at a time, and never skip the getaway. The silver grade reflects the repetition. The fifth job closed with a clean getaway is the one that fires the unlock.
steps: Find vault robbery opportunities
Complete each robbery
Escape the heat each time before counting it
trophies.hint: Each vault only counts once the escape is clean.
trophies.missable: Vault robberies are assumed to repeat, but the description does not confirm it; if vaults turn out to be limited events, schedule this trophy early rather than late.
trophies.verification: Count completed robbery-plus-escape runs yourself; the notification fires on the fifth.
sources: Official PlayStation trophy description: "Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape."
Atlas route phase 4 (Street Work & Heists) — bank vault robbery loop

Use the map's coverage indicators to see what is missing and turn the endgame into a targeted drive. The unlock fires when the last area registers. Pair it with the other map-sweep work to share the driving.

Cover towns, trails and waterways deliberately
Target the last areas with the coverage display

Learn where each gang operates, take one operation apiece, and tick the roster as you go. No performance condition applies. The last gang's robbery fires the unlock.

Rob one operation in each territory
Tick off the last gang on the roster

The only uncertainty is which venue qualifies, so try the most obvious beachfront spot on Ocean Beach before hunting alternatives. Order the drink, take the seat facing the water, and let the moment play. If nothing happens, the next venue along the strip is the next guess.

Order a cocktail
Stay seated with the view while the scene plays

Line up the glass front
Drive out through it at speed

Keep it on the watch list during partner trophies

Do not grind it deliberately; engage decision points as they come and check the tracker late in the run. If a shortfall remains, sweep whatever repeatable choice points the game still offers. The count itself is the only requirement.

Let the count accumulate across the campaign
Check the tracker late and sweep what remains

Story mission retries are the natural stage, since a wipe followed by a completion is a qualifying pair under the plain reading. Do not engineer failures recklessly; the game hands one out for free eventually. When that pattern occurs, the trophy tends to announce itself before you have finished celebrating the recovery.

Retry it immediately
Succeed on the second attempt
